task_name: The read of gate 1, and the key only the page gets

rubric.result: The objective promises two things. (a) 'GET /spec-freeze answers gate 1's state': SpecFreezeRoute.reading answers all four bodies the task names — {status:'none'} when held.held() is null and before the read is asked; {status:'no-spec'}; the draft body with spec path and the findings array; and the frozen body with 'on' and 'pullRequest' — dispatched over SpecFreezeState with a never-typed exhaustiveness guard. The repository and root come out of holding.conversation exactly as the task says, so the page sends no parameters. (b) 'hands a key that only a request coming from the page this backend serves ever receives': GateKey mints one hex key at construction (random(BYTES).toString('hex')) and forThePage delegates the decision to Browsers.isOurOwnPage(origin, host) rather than reimplementing it; the route spreads `key` into the draft body only when forThePage returned non-null. I confirmed at backend/src/infrastructure/http.ts:65-69 that isOurOwnPage requires origin === `http://${host}` over a loopback host, so a caller sending no Origin gets null. Nothing mounts the path in api-server.ts, but that is Task 9's own objective and Files line ('Wiring gate 1 into the server it runs in'), so it is not owed here.

The TDD line asks for `it('the read hands the gate key only to a request carrying the page own origin')` through a real listening server: the same draft read twice, once with Origin: http://127.0.0.1:<port> and once with none, the first body carrying `key` and the second having no `key` field at all. The diff's test is that test, name for name. It builds one server on an ephemeral port, one draft spy and one GateKey, then fetches twice from that same port: `RunningApi.fetching(port, { Origin: RunningApi.ownOrigin(port) })` and `RunningApi.fetching(port)`. The first is asserted toEqual a body containing `key: Keys.MINTED`; the second toEqual the same body without a `key` entry — and vitest's toEqual fails on an extra defined property, so the absence is genuinely pinned rather than merely unasserted. Same assertion, same input pair, same expected values as the written phrase.

Both Contract blocks match name by name. gate-key.ts: `static readonly HEADER = 'x-gate-key'`, `static readonly BYTES = 32` (literal values as written), `forThePage(asked: { origin: unknown, host: unknown }): string | null` and `holds(offered: unknown): boolean` are verbatim; the constructor destructures `{ random }` out of the same `{ random: (size: number) => Buffer }` shape the block declares, which changes nothing for the caller and is the host idiom (SpecFreezeRead, ApiServer, CoordinatingConversation all destructure). spec-freeze-route.ts: `PATH = '/spec-freeze'`, `METHODS = 'GET, POST'`, `static reading(held: CoordinatingSessions, read: ReadSpecFreeze, key: GateKey): RequestHandler` and `static refuseOtherMethods(request: Request, response: Response): void` are verbatim, parameter names and order included. The four wire bodies match the task's literal JSON, including `key` present only when minted and `pullRequest` carried as {number, url}. No Final text block and no Call site block in this task.

The rows this diff bears on: D-22 (the gates are the human's) is the row this task implements half of, and it implements it with the value the row states — the key is minted per run, lives only in memory, never reaches a prompt, a repository file or an environment, and is handed out only when Browsers.isOurOwnPage holds, so a session curling loopback with no Origin receives a body with no `key` field. D-10 (everything new under backend/ is TypeScript) — both new modules and the test are .ts with erasable syntax only, and typecheck is green. D-11 (a yardstick is imported from the plugin, never reimplemented) — the route forms no opinion about freezability; it hands out whatever findings ReadSpecFreeze gave, and EpicSpec#findings() is what calls the plugin's analyzeSpecFreeze. D-13 (no phase is stored) — the route stores nothing; every body is derived from held() and the query. I note without making it a finding that a session could still forge an Origin header and obtain the key; the plan closed that in Task 7's own text ('A session curling loopback sends no Origin, so it never gets the key') and fixed the mechanism in the Contract block by routing the decision through Browsers.isOurOwnPage, so the diff implements the value the row and the plan state. No row is reopened.

Exemplars: spec-freeze-route.ts is coordinating-session-route.ts's idiom line for line — a `reading(...)` static returning a RequestHandler, an early return for the held-nothing case, a private #answer dispatching over the frozen state constant with `const exhaustive: never` in the default, and an identical refuseOtherMethods setting Allow and answering 405 {code, detail}. The test is coordinating-session-route.test.ts's idiom: a Spy subclassing the real use case with the real port base classes in super(), a Mother of named scenarios, a RunningApi holding the servers with afterEach stopAll, real fetch against a listening server. defects.md, rule by rule: (1) closed vocabulary — SpecFreezeState and FreezeFindingCode are frozen catalogues, the dispatch is exhaustive and its default is a compile-time never guard that throws rather than a silent catch-all; no value that classifies anything is held as a loose string or a boolean; forThePage's `string | null` is an absent value, not an absent member of a vocabulary, and the Contract block fixed that signature anyway. (2) raw map as the return value of logic — #wireFindingOf returns a named readonly WireFinding and the response payloads are object literals built at the last step and handed to Answer.send, which sets a header and stringifies and decides nothing; no map crosses two of our own functions to be read by key lookup, so this is the sanctioned serialization boundary. (3) two fields that have to agree — this diff introduces none; there is no sentinel, no empty string for absence, no flag repeating another field. The state/nullable-spec pair that forces `outcome.spec!` lives in SpecFreezeRead, created in Task 5 and only consumed here, and the non-null assertion is the host's own idiom (holding.session! in the exemplar). (4) errors named for what happens, not where — the only throw is `no spec freeze answer declared for ${exhaustive}`, named for what happened and worded like the exemplar's; no error class is introduced and none is named for a module. style.md: no comment or docstring anywhere in the diff, every identifier and test name English, and no free function at module level — Keys.RANDOM, Mother, RunningApi and the two production classes all hang off a type. architecture.md: dependency direction respected (infrastructure imports application and domain, never the reverse); one controller per endpoint with its projection travelling in the same module; GateKey earns its own module because ct-api.ts constructs it in Task 9 and both handlers consume it, and the plan's Files line fixes the path. boundaries.md: the dependencies arrive as arguments (reading(held, read, key)) and GateKey takes `random` injected, so this module assembles nothing and the constructor is the seam; the outward projection is exhaustive and the refusal keeps {code, detail} in kebab-case with the protocol's own 405, which is what backend/conventions/this-repository.md's 'Answering HTTP in this API' prescribes. Delivery: the change is purely additive — two new modules and a new test, no signature altered, no public contract changed, no call site left on an old path — and no document of either yardstick prescribes a shape for that. Skills named by §3: control-tower-loop:test-driven-development and its testing-anti-patterns.md loaded and applied under item 9; backend-engineering:backend-best-practices loaded — it is a router over Python/Django/FastAPI references and, per backend/conventions/this-repository.md's precedence list ('it yields to both'), its headings that could bear here (hexagonal layers, value objects, mothers, mocking ports) are already the travelling yardstick's, and the diff conforms to them; frontend-engineering:frontend-best-practices has no subject in a diff with no frontend file. Two clashes declared rather than reported, because the implementer could not satisfy both sides: GateKey.holds() and GateKey.HEADER have no caller in the tree today (Task 8 adds them) and SpecFreezeRoute.reading has no production caller until Task 9 mounts it, which simplicity.md's 'which call breaks without it?' would ask about — but the Contract block prescribes both members verbatim and the Files line forbids touching api-server.ts here, so omitting them would be an item-3 defect instead. Third, minor and not a finding: key.forThePage is computed on every request and consumed only in the draft branch.

Does not apply. The diff's only test file, backend/__tests__/infrastructure/spec-freeze-route.test.ts, is new (new file mode 100644) and carries no `-` line. The only `-` lines in the whole diff are two lines of prose in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-14-issue-329-gate-1-the-freeze.md, which is plan text and contains no assertion, case or test. No pre-existing test was removed, relaxed or rewritten, here or anywhere else in the diff.

The behaviour the objective promises is produced by production code, not by the test's scaffolding. The four bodies come out of SpecFreezeRoute.#answerRead in backend/src/infrastructure/spec-freeze-route.ts, and the key decision comes out of GateKey.forThePage delegating to Browsers.isOurOwnPage in the already-existing http.ts — the test doubles neither: it doubles only ReadSpecFreeze (the use case, by construction, which is what testing.md's controller row prescribes) and injects a deterministic `random`, and it feeds the route real EpicSpec and FreezeFinding instances rather than models of them. The one place to look hardest, since this task is D-22's mechanism, is whether the boundary is asserted by construction: it is not. The test mounts Browsers.turnAwayForeign in front of the real handler, exactly as Task 9's Call site block will mount it, and the pair of requests differs only in the Origin header the real isOurOwnPage reads; make forThePage always return the key and the second assertion fails, make it always return null and the first does. Keys.MINTED is derived from the injected random bytes ('07' repeated BYTES times) rather than pasted, so it pins the hex encoding the production line performs. Reverting spec-freeze-route.ts and gate-key.ts leaves the test unable to import, let alone pass.

Inside the three backend files the diff writes only what the task asks for: gate-key.ts carries GateKey and its four contract members and nothing else; spec-freeze-route.ts carries PATH, METHODS, reading, the two private helpers that build the four bodies, and refuseOtherMethods; the test carries exactly the five tests the **Tests:** line names, plus the Spy, Mother and RunningApi that testing.md requires. No refactor, no rename, no adjacent fix, and nothing that touches what ### Out of scope names — groom.js and slices.js are not imported, no merge or pull-request write appears, and start-plan/implement-plan are untouched. The fourth path is the plan file, which the rubric makes an amendment for me to rule on rather than a path out of scope. I read the hunk line by line: it is four lines inside Task 6's prose and nothing else — 'the same method Task 5's query asks' becomes 'which wraps the same findings() Task 5's query reads'. It touches no **Files:**, **Tests:**, **TDD:** or **Verification:** line of Task 7 or of any other task, removes no route and disarms no control. I verified the substance myself rather than taking it on trust: backend/src/application/queries/read-spec-freeze.ts:72 calls spec.findings() and never isFreezable(), while backend/src/domain/value-objects/epic-spec.ts:76-78 defines isFreezable() as findings().length === 0 — so the sentence that left was false and the one that arrived is true. A correction of the record that changes no obligation and that could not ride in Task 6's own commit is justified, so this item holds.

Five new tests, all three properties held. Deterministic: the server listens on port 0 on 127.0.0.1 so no fixed port is assumed, randomness enters as an injected `random` rather than randomBytes, no clock or today's date is read (the frozen date is a literal on the spy's answer), no sleep and no path outside the process. Isolated: each test builds its own CoordinatingSessions, its own spy and its own server, and afterEach splices and closes every server started, so nothing survives into the next test and none of them depends on the order of the file. Verifies real behaviour: every assertion is on the status and the literal JSON body that came back over a real socket from the production handler, plus `read.asked` being empty on the two refused paths — testing.md's 'a refusal never reaches a double' — and none of them asserts a mock's call count or a constant the test just defined. The finer half, measured with control-tower-loop:test-driven-development and its testing-anti-patterns.md, which both loaded: no assertion on a mock's existence (anti-pattern 1); no test-only method added to a production class (anti-pattern 2) — GateKey.holds and HEADER are the next task's production API, not the test's; the doubles preserve the side effects the tests need, and ReadSpecFreezeSpy.neverAsked() throws when asked rather than answering silently (anti-pattern 3); Mother.PULL_REQUEST carries every field of the real ReviewedPullRequest shape (anti-pattern 4). The two names carrying 'and' would invite the skill's 'One behavior... "and" in name? Split it', but those names are the plan's own literal text in **TDD:** and **Tests:**, so they are the plan's call and not the implementer's; and the mother/spy scaffolding being longer than the test bodies is testing.md's requirement, not a defect. Nothing left to report at any severity.
